victim_compensation.notes: Pays up to $15,000 for crime-related costs not covered by insurance or other sources. Apply within 1 year of the crime and report it to police within 72 hours; late filing needs written good cause.
victim_compensation.issue: Max award was $30,000; the Commission's site states $15,000 (as of July 9, 2020); mailing address is a P.O. box, and the unsourced 'income not a factor' claim was dropped.

victim_compensation.notes: Pays up to $40,000 per victim ($80,000 total when a death leaves several dependents). Apply within 2 years of the crime and report it to police within 5 days unless that was not reasonably possible.
victim_compensation.issue: URL was doa.alaska.gov/vccb and address was a Fairbanks office; the Board is in the Dept. of Public Safety at vccb.alaska.gov, Anchorage. Max award taken from statute as quoted by CAP; not shown on the Board's site.

victim_compensation.program_name: Arizona Crime Victim Compensation Program (ACJC; applications through county attorney's offices)
victim_compensation.notes: Apply through the County Attorney's Office in the county where the crime happened; each county has its own phone number. The program pays only after insurance and other sources.
victim_compensation.issue: No statewide phone exists: claims are handled by the 15 county attorney's offices. The ACJC page does not state a max award or filing deadline, so $25,000 and 2 years could not be verified.

victim_compensation.notes: Pays up to $10,000, or up to $25,000 for catastrophic injury. Apply within 1 year and report the crime within 72 hours (the 72-hour rule does not apply to minors).
victim_compensation.issue: URL arcvr.com is not the official site; the Board is administered by the Arkansas Department of Public Safety.

victim_compensation.notes: Pays up to $70,000 per application. Apply within 7 years of the crime; victims who were minors have until 7 years after turning 21 (age 28), and late applications can be accepted for good cause.
victim_compensation.issue: Deadline was 3 years; CalVCB states 7 years from the crime (longer for minors).

victim_compensation.program_name: Colorado Crime Victim Compensation (run by each judicial district; overseen by DCJ Office for Victims Programs)
victim_compensation.notes: Colorado has no single statewide claims office: apply to the compensation program in the judicial district where the crime happened. Limits and rules are set by each district board.
victim_compensation.issue: Program is decentralized across judicial districts; the statewide phone (303) 239-4442, $30,000 max and 1-year deadline are not stated on the official page.

victim_compensation.program_name: Connecticut Judicial Branch Office of Victim Services
victim_compensation.notes: Pays up to $15,000 for personal injury and up to $25,000 to dependents of a homicide victim. Apply within 2 years of the crime; the deadline can be waived in some cases, and the crime must be reported to police.
victim_compensation.issue: Phone (860) 747-4501 not confirmed; the state lists OVS toll-free 1-888-286-7347. Program's own page (jud.ct.gov/crimevictim) could not be read, so URL set to the Judicial Branch home.

victim_compensation.program_name: Delaware Victims' Compensation Assistance Program (VCAP), Department of Justice
victim_compensation.address: 900 N King St, Suite 4, Wilmington, DE 19801
victim_compensation.notes: Pays up to $25,000 (up to $50,000 for permanent total disability). Apply within 1 year of the crime and report it to police within 72 hours; VCAP can extend or waive these limits.
victim_compensation.issue: URL cjc.delaware.gov/vcap is not current; VCAP is part of the Delaware Department of Justice.

victim_compensation.program_name: Crime Victims Compensation Program, D.C. Superior Court
victim_compensation.address: Court Building A, 515 5th St NW, Room 109, Washington, DC 20001
victim_compensation.notes: Pays up to $25,000 per claim. Apply within 1 year of the crime (or of learning about the program) and report the crime to police within 7 days.
victim_compensation.issue: URL path was not the court's page; deadline exception (1 year from learning of program) and 7-day police report rule added.
